contributions.title: Adoption narrative for candidate 3d637c8. The problem it solves: create_escrow accepted deposit_amount 0, so an escrow could be created whose vault held nothing; take_and_close then moved zero mint_a, still emitted CompleteEvent, and the taker paid rent on two init_if_needed accounts and received no

alternatives: Alternative considered and rejected: enforce the rule in the frontend create flow only. Rejected because the instruction is the trust boundary - any client, script or program can call create_escrow directly, and the empty escrow would remain creatable.

Alternative considered and rejected: impose a dust floor above the rent of the two init accounts instead of rejecting only zero. Rejected as a policy number rather than a defect fix, and it needs an owner decision on the threshold.

Alternative considered and rejected: guard the settlement side by rejecting a zero-balance vault inside take_and_close. Rejected because it leaves the empty escrow creatable and its maker's rent locked with no settlement path.

Alternative considered and deliberately not taken: extend the same rejection to maker_expected_price. Zero may be intended gift semantics - an airdrop that asks nothing in return - so guarding it is a product decision, not this defect.

Implementation variant noted: the guard uses Anchor's require_neq! macro rather than a project-specific error variant, so a zero submission aborts with Anchor's generic constraint error rather than a named project error.
narrative.integration: Integration is a lab-side merge of the single commit 3d637c8 into the lab fork's main by whoever owns that repository; I coordinate and do not merge. Mechanically it needs no companion work: no account layout, seed, instruction signature or settlement code changes, so escrows created before the guard read and settle exactly as before, and the generated client IDL does not need regeneration because no instruction argument changed. The frontend create path passes deposit_amount straight through to the instruction, so after integration a zero submission surfaces as a program error instead of a silently empty escrow; the follow-up, not a blocker, is for that error to be rendered as a readable message rather than a raw Anchor code. The one gate I would insist on before or with the merge is a test: a case that submits deposit_amount 0 and asserts the create fails, plus a case at the smallest accepted nonzero deposit. The only validation record in the envelope is evidence id validation-run, and I report its fields as the record's, not as my verdict.
limitations: Narrative drafted by the Sol.College CTO agent; authoritative fields (commits, evidence, hashes) are assembled by code.
narrative.problem: Adoption narrative for candidate 3d637c8. The problem it solves: create_escrow accepted deposit_amount 0, so an escrow could be created whose vault held nothing; take_and_close then moved zero mint_a, still emitted CompleteEvent, and the taker paid rent on two init_if_needed accounts and received no tokens in return. The candidate rejects that input with one require at the instruction - three added lines in one file - leaving account structs, seeds, instruction signatures, state layout and the settlement path untouched, so escrows created before the guard behave exactly as before. No acceptance is claimed and I do not merge. Alternatives, integration, rollback, limitations and risks follow.
risks: The candidate adds no test and both create paths at the SHA use nonzero deposits, so the guard's behaviour on deposit_amount 0 - the error code, and whether any account survives the aborted create - is not established by the records I read.

The record for evidence id validation-run reads status completed and conclusion success, created 2026-11-22T17:53:06Z and updated 2026-11-22T17:58:53Z, with the candidate SHA in its title and jobs check-request, untrusted-validate and attest; the untrusted-validate steps include a build of the candidate and 'Solana runtime integration fixture on a local validator'. Those are the record's own fields, which I report without restating them as a verdict; the record does not itemise which assertions the fixture made.
Acceptance is not mine to give and is not claimed here: this narrative describes a candidate, not an adopted change.
Rollback reinstates the defect, and nothing in the envelope records who decides on a rollback, on a dust floor, or on a gift mode.
maker_expected_price remains unguarded by design; if a nonzero ask is required, that is a separate question for the orchestrator.
Whether the research issue under source id research motivates this change is not established by the envelope.
The evidence covers a localnet fixture only; no devnet or mainnet-cluster behaviour and no upgrade path are covered.
The commit is unsigned and authored by automation, so provenance rests on the PR body and the run record rather than on a signature.
narrative.rollback: Rollback is a revert of one commit: three added lines, one file, no schema, no migration, no data. There is no state to unwind, because the guard runs only at creation - escrows already created under it carry the same layout and settle through the same path after a revert. The cost of rolling back is that it reinstates the defect: the zero-deposit path returns, and with it the empty vault, the zero-value take that still emits CompleteEvent, and the taker's wasted rent. I would roll back only on a fixture failure attributable to the guard, or on a product decision that zero-deposit escrows must be creatable; in that second case the better move is to replace the rejection with an explicit dust floor or an explicit gift mode rather than revert wholesale, so the choice is visible in the code instead of implicit.
